INTRODUCTION
         I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry, having been authorized
by the Committee, hereby present this Eighty-sixth Report on Performance Review of Metal Scrap Trade Corporation
Ltd. (MSTC).
2.      The Committee on Industry constituted Sub-Committee for Ministry of Steel to examine the Performance Review
of Metal Scrap Trade Corporation Ltd. (MSTC). The Sub-Committee visited Kolkata on 17th to 20th July, 2001 and
interacted with the Management of Metal Scrap Trade Corporation Ltd. (MSTC).
3.      The Sub-Committee in its meeting held on 14th March, 2002 heard the Secretary, Ministry of Steel and official of
MSTC. The Report has been prepared on the basis of on the spot-study by the Sub-Committee-I for the Ministry of Steel
of Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry and interaction with the Secretary, Ministry of
Steel and officials of Metal Scrap Trade Corporation Ltd. (MSTC).
4.      The Sub-Committee in its meeting held on 8th August, 2002 considered and adopted the Report.
5.      The Committee at its meeting held on 9th August, 2002 considered and adopted the Report.
6.      The Report was presented to the Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha on 20th August, 2002 by the then Chairman, Shri
T.N. Chaturvedi.
 
NEWDELHI 
December 11, 2002
DR. P. C. ALEXANDER
Chairman,
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee
on Industry
 
REPORT
         MSTC Limited (formerly known as Metal Scrap Trade Corporation Ltd.) was incorporated as a Public Limited
Company under the Companies Act, 1956 on 9 th September, 1964. The status of the company underwent change in
February, 1974 to that of a subsidiary of Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL). In the year 1982-83, the corporation
was converted into a Government of India Company transferring the shares of SAIL to the President of India. It was the
Canalizing Agency for import of Carbon Steel Melting’s Scrap, Sponge Iron, Hot Briquette Iron and re-rolled scrap till
February, 1992. It was also the canalizing agency for import of ships for breaking till August, 1991. Presently, the
company undertakes disposal of ferrous and non-ferrous scrap arising from integrated steel plants under SAIL/RINL
etc. and disposal of scrap, surplus stores, etc. from other public sector undertakings and Government departments and
also import of ferrous and non-ferrous scarp, coke, finished steel and petroleum products. MSTC is the only Central
PSU under the Ministry of Steel to issue bonus shares.

2.3    The Committee notes that the company has an authorised Capital of Rs.5 crore and paid up capital of Rs.2.20 crore
as on 31.3.2001 of which approximately 90 per cent of the shares are held by the President of India and the balance 10
per cent by the members of Steel Furnaces Association of India and Iron & Steel Scrap Association on India and others.
The Committee recommends that MSTC management would take every step to ensure that capital restructuring of
MSTC take place in such a way that Return On Investment (ROI) is maximum.
3.0    MAIN ACTIVITIES
3.1    The Sub-Committee was informed that MSTC has manifold activities which include (i) import (ii) export (iii)
Supply of raw material to actual users (iv) supply of materials as parallel marketer and (v) Scrap/Obsolete/Surplus
disposal on behalf of plant organizations. The company has four wings for its activities namely 
(i) International marketing (ii) Domestic Marketing (iii) Management services and (iv) Finance/HRD. Head office
located at Kolkata, the company has four regional offices at Kolkata, New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and branch offices
located at Bangalore, Vizag, Bhopal, Vadodara, Rourkela, Bokaro, Surat and New Mangalore. The Company has two
major spheres of activities i.e. Domestic Marketing and International Marketing.
3.1.0Domestic Marketing
3.1.1While a subsidiary of SAIL, MSTC started acting as selling agent of IISCO, RSP, BSL for disposal of their scrap
arising and thus started its Domestic Marketing activity. In 1993, after being de-linked from SAIL, MSTC extended its
activities to other PSUs, Government departments etc. The objective of DM is to maximize availability of indigenous
scrap by including the principals to mobilize and sell their scrap arisings/rejected/ condemned/surplus/spares/capital
equipments etc. so that the same can be recycled. The disposal action is taken in such a manner that the maximum
possible price is realized in totally transparent manner by selling the materials through open tenders, public auctions etc.
This activity was given importance only after decanalisation. The annual volume of business that was Rs.210 crore in
1992-93 reached at Rs.600 crore in 2000-2001.

3.1.5The Sub-Committee was apprised of problems being faced by MSTC in disposal of melting scrap as a whole has
gone down due to increased production of HBI that reached around five million tonnes. Many PSUs and Government
departments have their own scrap disposal set up, therefore, they are extremely reluctant to give this job to MSTC;
Railways are a prime example. Private auctioneers charging a very low rate also affect MSTC’s operation.
3.1.6The Committee understand the compelling circumstances under which the MSTC changed its focus of activities
from acting as a selling agent of SAIL to that of maximising direct marketing (DM) when MSTC got de-linked from
SAIL in 1993. The Committee appreciates the change in strategy in post-decanalised phase of imports. The Committee
is pleased to observe the performance of MSTC in direct marketing and hopes that an all out efforts would be taken by
MSTC management to strengthen the marketing activities to improve upon financial performance to a new commanding
heights.
3.1.7The Committee understands the problems being faced by MSTC in carrying out business in a situation when
demand for melting scrap is going down due to increased production of HBI and also because of setting up of scrap
disposal unit set up by PSUs and other Government departments, MSTC management has to chalk out ‘new strategy’ to
combat the situation. The Committee feels that provided the Ministry of Steel adhere to the principle of generating an
atmosphere of inter-PSU cooperation and take concrete steps towards assisting MSTC in procuring work-order from
Government PSU, the problems of MSTC could be sorted out to a great extent. The Committee may be apprised about
the action taken by the Ministry in this direction.
3.2.0INTERNATIONAL MARKETING
3.2.1After decanalisation in February, 1992 and due to development of indigenous Direct Reduced Iron (DRI) industry,
the demand for imported scrap was considerably reduced in the country. MSTC’s volume of imports came down on
both the counts. The Company therefore enlarged its import basket and it now undertakes import of scrap on behalf of
large industrial houses such as ESSAR, Ispat Mukund, etc. on back to back basis and other items such as non-ferrous
scrap, petroleum products, superior kerosene oil, furnace oil, ferro alloys, slab end cuttings., DR Pellets, etc., as per the
need of actual users in the competition with other private parties.

3.2.4The Sub-Committee was apprised of difficulties in International Marketing for import of ferrous scrap for EAF/IF
units. Lower demand for scrap due to change in charge mix owing to increased availability of DRI and sponge iron.
Steel industry undergoing a demand recession coupled with arrival of imported finished steel at cheaper price.
International scrap price fluctuation; adverse exchange fluctuation as well as competition from private sector.
3.2.5The Committee is pleased to note the performance of MSTC in international marketing and appreciates the strategy
of MSTC management for enlarging its import basket in post decanalised phase to compete with other private parties
engaged in similar business.
3.2.6The Committee feels that with the revival of steel industry and undergoing process of strengthening of anti-
dumping the prospect of MSTC business in international market would lead to opening of new avenues.
3.2.7The Committee further hopes that MSTC management would chalk out strategy to ensure its survival while
working in adverse condition caused because of lower demand for scrap due to change in charge-mix-owing to
increased availability of DRI and sponge iron. MSTC has also to learn how to respond and work in a competitive
environment.
3.3.0MSTC AS A HOLDING COMPANY
3.3.1MSTC plays yet another role of a holding company of M/s Ferro Scrap Nigam Limited (FSNL) whose 60% shares
are held by MSTC and 40% by M/s Harsco Corporation Inc., USA. FSNL is engaged in salvaging and processing of
scrap for re-cycling in the SAIL steel plants and elsewhere. The net worth of the company as on 31.3.2000 was Rs.98.99
crore.
3.3.2The Committee notes the activities and responsibility of MSTC as a holding company.
4.0    MODERNISATION, RESTRUCTURING  AND EXPANSION PROGRAMMES OF MSTC
         The MSTC informed the Committee that efforts have been made for modernisation and expansion for
International Marketing Division and Domestic Marketing Division.
4.1    Modernisation of International Marketing Division
         As regards the modernisation of International Marketing Division following steps have been taken :-
              (i)    Identify material for which demand exists for imports;
              (ii)    Select  items;
              (iii)   Locate buyers;
              (iv)   Locate international sources;
              (v)   imports, preferably on back to back basis;
              (vi)   sell to traders or actual users; and
              (vii)  price disadvantage due to low utilization of capacity of EAF/IF units.
4.2    Modernisation of Domestic Marketing Division
         As regards the modernisation of Domestic Marketing Division following steps have been taken :-
              (i)    computerization through I.S.T.M.S. package;
              (ii)    Introduction of E-Auction;
              (iii)   Modernisation of international marketing;
              (iv)   Web-hoisting of purchase tenders; and
              (v)   placement  of contract, payment gateways.
4.3    Restructuring – Internal
         As regards internal restructuring of MSTC Sub-Committee was furnished following :-
              (i)    No long term debt is being envisaged;
              (ii)    sufficient working capital finance is available;
              (iii)   No plan for major capital expenditure in near future; and
              (iv)   No capital restructuring is envisaged in near future.
4.4    Expansion of Domestic and International Marketing Division
         For expansion of Domestic and International Marketing Division following strategy is being adopted :-
              (i)    Expansion of domestic marketing;
              (ii)    aggressive marketing large volume of purchase and sell;
              (iii)   move to selling agency for finished products; and
              (iv)   expansion of international marketing – (a) widen the import basket, (b) introduction of stock and sale.
4.5    Strategy for International Marketing
         The Sub-Committee was informed that MSTC has adopted following strategy for International Marketing:-

4.6    The Committee notes the steps taken by MSTC management in the field of modernisation, restructuring and
expansion programmes of MSTC. The Committee is of the view that although MSTC is not engaged in the process of
production and is a trading company, however, steps taken towards modernisation and restructuring would help in
improving its operational efficiency and managerial effectiveness. The Committee is of the firm view that
modernisation in the process and system of working of the company would have a definite bearing on the physical and
financial performance of the company. The steps taken to modernise and restructure the communication and expansion
in the domestic as well as international marketing division would yield positive fruits in the functioning of the company,
the Committee feels so. The Committee further feels that the efforts made on the part of MSTC management for
enlarging import basket would add to the profitability of the company.
5.0    PERFORMANCE OF MSTC
5.1    MSTC role is to canalize import to meet the demand for scrap from EAF Industries. As a subsidiary of SAIL,
MSTC started acting as selling agency for SAIL in respect of their metal scrap arising particularly from IISCO, RSP,
DSP and BSL. During 1982-1987 MSTC became an independent company under Ministry of Steel. SAIL started selling
melting scrap directly. MSTC started acting as selling agents to other PSUs and Government/ Departments. During
1987-1991 import of stainless steel scrap decanalized. Double window system effectively deregulated import of old
vessels. Introduction of Rep Licence which ends MSTC’s monopoly in imports of CSMS. Maximum PBT achieved by
MSTC was Rs.13.20 crore in 1988-1989.

5.3    The Sub-Committee was further informed that with the change of Government policies, imports were de-canalised
in February, 1992, thereafter, traders, shredders and users entered in the area of import of scrap and trade. As a result,
MSTC’s import of scrap continued to reduce since 1991-1992. In response to de-canalisation MSTC has taken
following steps:-
         (i)     DT strengthened sales increase from Rs.140 crore in 1990-1991 to Rs.498 crore in 1997-1998 (Rs.486 crore
in 1998-1999, Rs.600 crore in 2000-2001 and is expected to Rs.630 crore in 2001-2002);
         (ii)     Efforts to maintain a position of dominance in import of scrap end in a fiasco in 1995-1996, MSTC laden
with a stock of more than 1,00,000 tonnes costing above the market price. Import came to a standstill from
September, 1996 to March, 1998;
         (iii)    Desperate efforts to liquidate stock resulted in outstandings reaching a record high of about Rs.32 crore
presently under litigation;
         (iv)    Projects for investment with marketing/procurement rights identified investment made in KISCO,
investment in SJK under consideration; and
         (v)    Imports resumed with widened basket in 1997-1998, Rs.82 crore in 1998-1999, Rs.285 crore in 2000-2001.
The import was expected to cross Rs.300 crore mark in 2001-2002.
5.4    The Committee observes that the activities of MSTC has undergone noticeable change with the changing scenario
of steel industry, change in the Government policy i.e. from canalisation to the de-canalisation of imports and in
accordance with market perspective. The MSTC, which acted earlier as a selling agency for SAIL in respect of their
melting scrap arising, has started to carry the business with the other Government PSU when SAIL started selling
melting scrap directly. MSTC went, rightly, for strengthening of direct-marketing when the Government policy stood
for de-canalisation of import. Although the performance of MSTC suffered to some extent during these phase of
tumultuous change, however, it is the managerial skill which led MSTC for changing business gear and it is the
concerted employees’ commitment which has got a bearing on the physical and financial performance of the company.
The Committee acclaims the performance of MSTC and hopes that an all out effort on the part of the management and
employees would continue to improve the financial performance of the company to a new zenith.

10.0  PROCUREMENT OF WORKORDER FROM SAIL, RINL  AND RAILWAYS
10.1  The MSTC management stated that MSTC has been making constant efforts for getting business from SAIL and
RINL. But due to upgradation of technology, availability of scrap for disposal has been reduced. MSTC is, however,
striving to make marketing of semis and fixed products of the plants during 2001-2002. MSTC has already worked in
this direction.
10.2  Attempts have been made by MSTC on a number of occasions to get business from Railways. However, no
success could be achieved. In the latest round of efforts, a proposal was sent to Member, Engineering and Member,
Mechanical, Railway Board on 15.1.1999 and this was followed by personal visits. However, when no reply was
received, the matter was taken up through Ministry of Steel and the then Hon’ble Minister of Steel wrote to his
counterpart in Railway Ministry on 30.7.1999. This was followed by a letter to Chairman, Railway Board on 23.8.1999.
Ultimately that resulted in a meeting at the Railway Ministry on 24.5.2000 when a presentation was made. Thereafter,
as per suggestion of the Railways, MSTC officials visited various Railways and proposals were sent to Railway Board.
Since no response was coming from Railways, the matter was once again taken up through Steel Ministry and the
Minister of State for Steel has written to the Minister of Railways on 13.7.2001.
10.3  The CMD, MSTC management stated ----
“As far as business is concerned, MSTC could not make any breakthrough in the Railways scrap business in spite
of letters written by the Hon’ble Steel Minister to his counterpart in the Railways and in spite of the instructions by
the Railways and in spite of the instructions by the Railway Minister, nothing progressed. Therefore, he sought
help from the Committee to get the Railway business.”

was seen that the rates obtained by Railways were very low, hence MSTC has stopped taking part in tenders of
Railways. MSTC has indicated a service charge of 2 per cent to the Railways and has requested Railways to try MSTC
at least on a trial basis.
10.5  Replying to the Sub-Committee’s query regarding the role of the Ministry of Steel in helping MSTC in procuring
work order the Ministry stated that MSTC has gradually been attracting more customers through periodic
advertisements, personal contact etc. most of the central PSUs, having a reasonable volume of metal scrap arising, are
already doing business with MSTC. The e-auction portal which is being introduced, is also expected to attract more
customers. The Railway Board at present gets private auctioneers to conduct their auction at very low rates, which

use MSTC’s services (except for conducting a few auctions) as they manage bulk of their disposals departmentally.

11.0  HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT OF MSTC
11.1  The Committee was informed that MSTC’s volume of business in the current year is expected to be over Rs.
950.00 crore. This is being achieved with manpower of 280. Indisputably with more qualified and skilled
workforce, manpower can be reduced but at the moment there are surpluses in certain pockets and deficits in
others,. MSTC is, however concentrating on redeploying its existing workforce and also to utilize available
workforce fully by increasing the volume of business rather than in terms of separation. It is worthwhile to mention
that the volume of business, which stood at Rs. 497 crore in 1997-1998, is expected to Rs. 950 crore this year
without any increase in the manpower.

activities with a total manpower of 280. The Committee is pleased to note that MSTC management is adopting the

that MSTC is adhering to the principle of right man at right place at right time which would certainly help in
improving the performance of the company. The Committee also expects that MSTC management would examine
the labour productivity in term of turnover/sales/profit and in human resource as per requirement.

13.0  PROBLEMS BEING FACED BY MSTC
13.1  Sale Tax Structure
         13.1.1Pointing out the lacuna in the Sales Tax Structure, MSTC management informed the Sub-Committee that a
provision in the recent budget allows the State Governments to impose central sales tax on declared goods at
a rate higher than 4% and also empower them to impose multi-point tax. If the States use these powers, this
will make the job of trading extremely difficult, while a uniform system of VAT will be ideal, uniformity in
the matter of sales tax i.e. one point tax whether CST of LST, shall go a long way in helping traders
particularly the trading houses carrying on trading in more than State in the country.
         13.1.2The Committee understands the problems being faced by trading organisation due to prevalence of multi-
point tax-structure. Therefore, the Committee is of the view that the Ministry of Steel should take up the
matter with the Ministry of Finance and State Governments. The proposal of uniform system of VAT and
one-point tax may be examined and if found feasible, steps in this regard may be taken at the earliest.
13.2.0         Requirement of submission of end-use certificates for imported melting scrap
         13.2.1As regards the provision for requirement of submission of end-use certificates for imported melting scrap,
the Sub-Committee was informed that on import of melting scrap, the end use certificate is required to be
submitted by the actual users within six months. The main reason for this is to eliminate the misuse of scrap
imported for melting, being used for re-rolling. As a trader, MSTC sells such melting scrap to actual users
only but have to depend on the actual users to submit end-use certificate issues by Central Excise
Department after the melting scrap sold to them has been consumed. In the event of actual users’ failure to
obtain end-use certificate from the Central Excise, MSTC has to pay higher rate of duty on the material
imported. This requirement should, therefore, be withdrawn.
         13.2.2The Committee is of the opinion that the Government should evolve alternative effective mechanism to
check the misuse of scrap imported for melting, being used for re-rolling.

(Department of Excise) for withdrawing the provision for requirement of submission of end-users certificate
for imported melting scrap. If the Ministry of Finance remains unmoved the provision may be made for
early submission of end-use certificate by the actual users’ and in case of default, a certain the penalty may
be imposed on the defaulter. The Committee is of the view that MSTC should not be subjected to imposition
of higher rate of duty for the default committed by the actual users.
13.3.0         Requirement of availing services of trans-chart for hiring ships for imports
         13.3.1The Sub-Committee was apprised that as per existing procedure, PSUs are to import materials on FOB basis
and shipping arrangement is to be made through Ministry of Shipping (Trans-chart). In case Trans-chart is
unable to arrange shipping, necessary waiver is to be obtained by PSUs form Trans-chart before finalising
contract on C&F basis. Import contracts by MSTC are finalised at very short notice. Since it is seldom
possible to fix a vessel through Trans-chart in the short time available, MSTC is compelled to continue
imports on C&F basis for shipload cargoes. It would be in the fitness of things, especially in the liberalized
scenario, to do away with the requirement of approaching Trans-chart.
         13.3.2The Committee understands that since MSTC finalise import contracts usually in a short span of time so it is
difficult on the part of MSTC to fix a vessel through Ministry of Shipping (Trans-chart). Therefore, the
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Steel should take the matter with the Ministry of Shipping and
help MSTC out by doing away with the requirement of approaching Trans-chart.
13.3.3The Committee notes that MSTC is one of the few Government companies which has successfully withstood
the impact of post liberalization era by changing its strategy according to the need of the situation. The
Committee hopes that the Ministry of Steel would extend a helping hand to the company in sorting out its
problems so that it can fetch a better price from the prospective buyers.

MSTC is adhering to the principle of right man at right place at right time which would certainly help in improving the
performance of the company. The Committee also expects that MSTC management would examine the labour
productivity in term of turnover/Sales/profit and in human resource as per requirement.                                          (Para :
11.2)
SWOT ANALYSIS OF MSTC
         The Committee observes that MSTC management has given due importance to the significance of SWOT-analysis
in the general working of the company. The Committee appreciates MSTC management for adhering to the basic
principles and practice of management. The efforts of re-defining of SWOT-analysis on the part of MSTC management
to a praiseworthy step and the Committee hopes that MSTC management would continue to reorient its SWOT-analysis
on per changing industrial and economic scenario and chalk out its further strategy as per the commends of outcome of
SWOT-analysis.                                                                                                                            (Para : 12.3)
         The Committee is of the opinion that MSTC management should take advantage of its strength as the company has
minimal fixed overheads expenditure due to optimum manpower with expertise from SAIL, equipped with modern
telecommunication and computer. The Committee is pleased to note that MSTC has  good track record for executing
impacts contracts due to its goodwill in the domestic and international market. Banking upon its company,
goodwill/track-record, MSTC management should make efforts to enhance its market share in domestic as well as
international market.         (Para : 12.4)
         The Committee opines that with the induction of liberalisation policy bureaucratic procedures and regulation has
been done away with. However, MSTC management in tandem with the Ministry of Steel should point out in the ATN
of the present Report the bureaucratic hurdles and Government control having adverse imports on the marketing
capacity of MSTC. The Committee is of the opinion that MSTC management should have a re-look on the areas of
weakness in the SWOT analysis and should take adequate steps for overcoming its weaknesses i.e. induction of latest
technological developments, streamlining of the main activities positioning of right man at right place in right time,
redrafting of corporate goal in the internal market etc.                                                                                            (Para :
12.5)
         The Committee recommends that MSTC management would explore ways and means to capitalise on
opportunities for better financial performance of the Company and it is being hoped that the Ministry of Steel would
extend all possible help to MSTC in this regard. MSTC management may explore the possibilities of MSTC entering
into domestic/international joint venture strategic alliance, explore new governess for activities of the company and
consequent changes in the object clearance of the company in order to infect synergy in the overall working of the
company.  (Para : 12.6)
         The Committee further recommends that MSTC management should chalk out strategy for getting rid of threats

being faced by the company. MSTC management may undertake required steps to inject resilience in the working of the

PROBLEMS BEING FACED BY MSTC
Sale Tax Structure
         The Committee understands the problems being faced by trading organisation due to prevalence of multi-point
tax-structure. Therefore, the Committee is of the view that the Ministry of Steel should take up the matter with the
Ministry of Finance and State Governments. The proposal of uniform system of VAT and one-point tax may be
examined and if found feasible, steps in this regard may be taken at the earliest.                                                  (Para :
13.1.2)
REQUIREMENT OF SUBMISSION OF END-USE CERTIFICATES FOR IMPORTED MELTING SCRAP
         The Committee is of the opinion that the Government should evolve alternative effective mechanism to check the
misuse of scrap imported for melting, being used for re-rolling.                                         (Para : 13.2.2)
         The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Steel should approach the Ministry of Finance (Department of
Excise) for withdrawing the provision for requirement of submission of end-users certificate for imported melting scrap.
If the Ministry of Finance remains unmoved the provision may be made for early submission of end use certificate by
the actual users’ and in case of default, a certain the penalty may be imposed on the defaulter. The Committee is of the
view that MSTC should not be subjected to imposition of higher rate of duty for the default committed by the actual
users.         (Para : 13.2.3)
REQUIREMENT OF AVAILING SERVICES OF TRANS-CHART FOR HIRING SHIPS FOR IMPORTS
         The Committee understands that since MSTC finalise import contracts usually in a short span of time so it is
difficult on the part of MSTC to fix a vessel through Ministry of Shipping (Transchart). Therefore, the Committee
recommends that the Ministry of Steel should take the matter with the Ministry of Shipping and help MSTC out by
doing away with the requirement of approaching Transchart.                                                                           (Para :
13.3.2)
         The Committee notes that MSTC is of one of the few Government, companies which has successfully withstood
the impact of port liberalization era by changing its strategy according to the need of the situation. The Committee
hopes that the Ministry of Steel would extend a helping hand to the company in sorting out its problems so that it can
fetch a better price from the prospective buyers.                                                                                           (Para : 13.3.3)
